::: {.callout-note}
## TL;DR
Add seated/standing mode with height calibration and a persistent comfort and accessibility options menu (vignette, turn mode, locomotion, captions, input remapping), then check on device that every option holds the target frame rate and breaks nothing.
:::

## Lab Overview

**Duration**: 2 hours
**Hardware**: Meta Quest 3 / 3S (Quest 2 acceptable)
**Software**: Unity 2022 LTS, XR Interaction Toolkit 2.x, Meta XR SDK
**Deliverable**: Lab journal entry + Unity scene (uploaded to VLE)

---

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this lab you will be able to:

- Implement seated mode with height and reach calibration
- Build a comfort and accessibility options menu that persists between sessions
- Verify comfort options on device without regressing performance or function

---

## Part 1: Calibration (35 min)

### Task 1.1

Add a seated/standing toggle and a height calibration step.

### Task 1.2

Verify that all interactive content remains reachable in seated mode.

## Part 2: Options Menu (50 min)

### Task 2.1

Build a persistent options menu exposing vignette strength, turn mode, locomotion type and caption visibility.

### Task 2.2

Save settings between sessions and apply them at startup.

### Task 2.3

Add remappable input for at least the primary interaction.

## Part 3: Regression Test (35 min)

### Task 3.1

Re-measure frame time with each comfort option enabled, using the profiling method from the Week 11 lab. A vignette that drops frames is not a comfort feature.

### Task 3.2

Test every option combination on device and confirm nothing has broken.

---

## Checkpoint

A working accessibility and comfort options menu, verified on device and holding the target refresh rate, ready for peer evaluation in Week 12.
